newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour will seek public consent on EMU - Blair.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour will seek public consent on EMU - Blair.

text.p: British opposition Labour leader Tony Blair repeated on Wednesday that a Labour government would seek the consent of the people before taking any decision on joining a European single currency, but he stopped short of promising a referendum.

"If you're going to take a step as significant as the single currency then you have to have the consent of the people, whether that is though a general election or whether through referendum," he said in an interview with BBC radio.

But when asked if it was likely the British people would be able to express their opinion without a referendum, Blair said, "We'll have to see what happens in the run up to a general election and the issues that are there before the people."

He said Labour would decide whether or not to join on the basis of the national economic interest. "And it is important to recognise that to rule out a single currency for ever would be a serious mistake."
But Blair sounded a note of caution on EMU, saying to join would force the UK to give up some control over the economy.

"I believe it is a very, very significant economic step and if you give up means of adjustment in your economy of the exchange rate and you don't have, as we won't have, the possibility of compensating for the changes in economic convergence through fiscal transfers or labour mobility, then you have to take account of these economic facts when you take the decision."
